title: Build-time catalogue static export (deterministic snapshot of the 10 read-only /catalogue GETs)
increment: Render the ten /catalogue GET routes into versioned static JSON artefacts a static host can serve, plus a manifest. Parameterised routes are enumerated over the same query helpers the live handlers use; /search and /compare are exported as the full published-offer corpus in the live item shape (client-side query runs in slice 2). Currency is REUSED, not reimplemented: one unscoped queries.currency_context(now=as_of) shared by every artefact, byte-equivalent to each handler's scoped context. Ship a CLI (python -m app.export) and thin ps1/sh wrappers. Do NOT touch apps/web.
acceptance: Every artefact and the manifest carry an explicit injected as_of; the wall clock is read only at the CLI boundary.

Exported data encodes staleness: a stale/unknown claim serialises with collapsed confidence_label, freshness null (or measured 0.0 for checked-but-expired), and evidence_currency.current=false, so a renderer cannot present it as fresh.
Unknown stays unknown: uncheckable evidence is checked=false, current=false, freshness=null; an absent field is absent, not free.
Per-source staleness windows in the manifest are derived via reconcile.parse_schedule_window (2x cadence, e.g. 2d/2h), never one global figure.
Deterministic: same DB state + same as_of yields byte-identical output, demonstrated by building twice and diffing (not asserted).
Route parity: for the 8 concrete routes the artefact data equals the live handler .model_dump(mode='json') at the same pinned clock; /search and /compare corpora contain every live item verbatim.
New tests proven load-bearing by mutating their SUBJECT; positive controls present for count/absence claims; ruff check and ruff format --check clean; collected test counts stated.
enumeration_decision: Providers over queries.fetch_providers (ordered by slug); offers over every queries.is_published offer sorted by id. Each instance fetched via the same query helper the live handler uses. Manifest lists slugs/ids + counts as a positive control (a broken enumerator returns empty, which counts expose).
search_compare_decision: Both are queries, not resources; a static host cannot execute an arbitrary keyword search or id-tuple compare. Export the FULL published-offer corpus in the exact live item shape (search: union of all unfiltered pages; compare: every offer's server-normalised compare cell). kind='corpus' + a note. Each corpus item still carries its own evidence_currency frozen at as_of. Slice 2 runs the query client-side.
currency_reuse_decision: REUSED, not reimplemented. The export calls queries.currency_context + app.read_api.service serializers, so the same confidence_label collapse, freshness->null withholding, and evidence_currency block are baked in. One unscoped whole-catalogue context is byte-equivalent to each handler's scoped context because a version's verdict depends on its own evidence alone (fetch_evidence_currency contract). Pinned by the route-parity test.
measurement_limit: Integration tests are DATABASE_URL-gated. They were EXECUTED against the local populated Postgres (not merely shipped for CI): 7 collected, 7 passed (no exit-5 empty collection). The shared populated corpus is why ~50 unrelated integration tests fail environmentally on this tree; those are pre-existing and not caused here.
